source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Brain imaging is obtained mainly to determine the client's blood type before reperfusion, because transfusion compatibility determines eligibility for thrombolysis.","B":"Brain imaging is obtained mainly to confirm that every ischemic stroke is already visible, because absence of an infarct on early imaging excludes acute stroke.","C":"Brain imaging is essential to exclude intracranial hemorrhage before reperfusion therapy, because hemorrhage would change management and make thrombolysis unsafe.","D":"Brain imaging is used mainly to identify chronic neurologic disease before treatment, because excluding acute hemorrhage is not necessary when onset is witnessed."}}
source_row.rationale: The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline states that brain imaging is essential before reperfusion therapy to exclude intracranial hemorrhage; noncontrast CT can rapidly detect acute bleeding. Option C states that purpose. Option A incorrectly makes blood typing the reason for brain imaging. Option B incorrectly requires a visible early infarct to confirm ischemic stroke. Option D incorrectly says acute hemorrhage need not be excluded when the onset time is known.
source_row.source_detail: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke — Emergency brain imaging/reperfusion evaluation: brain imaging is essential before acute reperfusion therapy to exclude intracranial hemorrhage; noncontrast CT rapidly detects acute hemorrhage. AHA/ASA 2026 acute ischemic stroke guideline, current in 2026; currentness rechecked after the July 2026 guideline correction on 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, medical emergencies and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: AHA/ASA — 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
source_row.stem: A client presents 90 minutes after sudden focal neurologic deficits and is being considered for reperfusion therapy. Why is urgent brain imaging obtained before treatment?
